analytic_review_groups: Relative pole conventions and minimal type are distinguished from scalar and potential uniqueness; fixed-reference exponential moments supply the relative bound.
Zero-parameter domination uses contact with a strict stretch, finite-level subtraction and a positive-volume compactness contradiction, including infinite-mass competitors.
The big-background Lp construction keeps the integrability exponent q separate from the exponential exponent gamma; contact partitions give the exact weighted equation without an extra factor.
Bounded stability allows the unbounded comparison member and optimizes the small and large density errors with the stated endpoint exponent.
Kiselman regularization uses an independently fixed minimizing radius, curvature repair and gradient bound to obtain exactly the stated Holder exponent.
Local big-background continuity repairs curvature with a strict barrier and only claims continuity away from the barrier poles.
Homogeneous local Dirichlet solutions have uniform boundary and translation barriers; decreasing ellipticity yields the zero determinant equation, without a global mass assertion.
Continuous obstacle contact uses a local homogeneous replacement and a strict boundary gap to force zero measure away from contact.
General contact separates upper capping and the two lower truncations; weighted capacity limits exhaust infinite extended measures away from poles.
Relative compactness uses summable translated roofs and weighted lower semicontinuity; the lower-bound-only variant preserves its weaker singularity conclusion.
Bounded subsolutions regularize in a fixed smooth background; mixed density inequalities are applied to smooth-volume measures before bounded-product limits.
Weighted addition truncates the finite forcing measure and identifies equations on fixed finite levels before passing to the unrestricted measure.
The relative density norm has a positive lower bound in the remaining background; the zero forcing case does not supply a uniform total-mass bound.
Prescribed existence separates normalized scalar bounds, relative uniform estimates, common-barrier capacity convergence and uniqueness of the scalar.
Big minimal comparison localizes away from the strict barrier poles and does not assume a minimum of a discontinuous difference is attained.
Big reference stability builds convex subsolutions and uses a global Gauduchon trace to bound scalars without bounded total mass.
Big minimal existence proves pairwise stability before identifying the limiting equation, with density compactness and local bounded-product convergence.
Big minimal Holder regularity uses the fixed barrier and envelope normalization; symmetry is treated independently of an arbitrary choice of barrier.

Nonclosed interior smoothness uses the complete proper-gap dependency, local comparison, measurable concave elliptic extensions, trace and boundary estimates, polynomial regularization bounds, and the final C1-alpha iteration.

Semipositive degeneration obtains uniform scalar and trace bounds, smooth convergence off the exceptional locus, nodal integrability thresholds, closed-case energy uniqueness and both intrinsic-diameter hypotheses for metric completion.

Symmetric equation selection reconstructs a third invariant solution; weak flux regularity is proved rather than inferred from bounded variation, and the contact bands retain their exact C1,1/C2 boundary.
The NUMA canonical limit distinguishes closed-case uniqueness from the general approximation limit and preserves the geometric hypotheses.
Positive-exponent NUMA regularity keeps local bounds and the required limiting equation separate from global uniqueness.
Local-density boundary examples check the logarithmic integrability, polar-set extension of bounded products, compact gluing, failure of every Lp estimate and the constant-density Lipschitz example.
Resolved ordinary equations track the Jacobian, bounded-remainder descent, closed uniqueness and the actual residual metric-completion behavior.

Exceptional minimal equations preserve the fixed original curvature metric: the smooth sigma correction gives the same background, the Kahler barrier uses the chosen auxiliary curvature, and iterated blowups use total exceptional divisors and auxiliary logarithms.

A relative measure carrier is built from countably many finite-level local carriers with summable coefficients; extended domination and the Radon--Nikodym density do not assume finite total Monge--Ampere mass.
The bounded carrier retains its stronger bounded hypothesis and does not extend boundedness to the general relative construction.
Lower-mass solvability keeps scalar order, density continuity, dense nonsolvable data at zero lower mass and the separately proved general-measure criterion distinct.
The individual threshold is attained as a lower measure inequality via truncation and closure, without claiming equality, finite mass or convergence in capacity.
The greatest threshold envelope follows from maximum stability and compactness, without adding uniqueness of arbitrary threshold potentials.
Integrable Gauduchon tests check the dense zero-threshold example, the dual root functional, monotone truncations and exact metric/gauge/volume transformations.
Zero-lower-mass product equations calculate the sublogarithmic radial flux, exact scalar sandwich and finite-mass envelope class; the nonclosed factor remains essential.
Closed-factor equations solve arbitrary integrable data with zeros and compute the exact product threshold without asserting closure for all product data.

Continuous-potential product measures use Green-kernel continuity, strong Sobolev smoothing and a canonical measure trace; variational uniqueness and zero-exponent selection concern the closed curve or separated class.
Individual density stability proves upper semicontinuity, identifies zero-threshold continuity points and establishes the root norm and its completeness at the precise mass boundary.
Uniform root tails characterize the closed order ideal; clipping, dominated convergence in measure and smooth density retain the stated norm topology.
Closed-factor roots give an isometric image and the exact integrable tail, without adding any higher Lr moment.

Individual exponential equations prove greatest-solution existence, scalar and measure selection, zero-threshold concentration and exponent-interval limits; two-sided continuity outside the countable jump set is explicitly restricted to interior exponents.
The exponential tail modulus retains its quantitative root-tail bound, while an Lr assumption supplies the linear rate; the order ideal alone supplies no such rate or potential compactness.

Radial integrable selection checks smooth density truncation, separated greatest solutions and mass-one flux, joint limits at arbitrary relative rates, capacity convergence, the exact moment threshold and scalar divergence, and order only in the separated closed class.
